title: Dangerous Goods Acceptance: lead time of a declaration before the scheduled departure
content:
## Rule
For the late declaration fee under the Dangerous Goods Acceptance product, the lead time of the judged declaration is the number of calendar days from the date on which the shipper signed it to the scheduled departure date (ETD) recorded on the booking carrying the goods. The declaration is on time when that lead time is at least the category's declaration lead time and late when it is fewer. An acceptance whose booking shows no scheduled departure owes no late fee.

## Declaration lead time by category
| Category | Declaration lead time (calendar days before ETD) |
|---|---|
| AHL DG Limited Quantity | 3 |
| AHL DG Class 9 Standard | 5 |
| AHL DG Flammables and Corrosives | 7 |
| AHL DG Toxics and Oxidizers | 7 |
| AHL DG Compressed Gases | 10 |
| AHL DG Special Approval | 21 |

## Input → judgement → outcome
Signing date of the judged declaration, and ETD of the booking carrying the goods → count the calendar days from the first to the second → compare with the category's lead time → at least the lead time: on time; fewer: late. No ETD on the booking → no late fee.

## Boundary cases (AHL DG Flammables and Corrosives, lead time 7 days; hypothetical dates)
| Signed on | ETD of the booking | Lead time | Judgement |
|---|---|---|---|
| 13 June | 20 June | 7 days | on time — 7 is at least 7 |
| 14 June | 20 June | 6 days | late — 6 is fewer than 7 |
| 20 June | 20 June | 0 days | late |
| 13 June | none recorded | — | no late fee |

## Points of judgement
- *Is the lead time measured to the cargo cut-off?* No; it is measured to the ETD recorded on the booking carrying the goods.
- *A lead time exactly equal to the category's figure — on time or late?* On time; the declaration is late only when the lead time is fewer.
